name: Switzerland
headline: Switzerland: +1.6% growth in 2025, 0.2% inflation, debt 40% of GDP
sections: Switzerland is a $1.06 trillion economy (2025), the world's 21st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.6% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $103K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 18.9% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.2% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 2.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.8% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 40% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 45% in 2020. The general government balance is +0.2% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +5.6% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 147% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 36% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 84.4 years (2024). Population: 9.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
